about: One topic the runner and the server write the same way (contracts/wiki.contract.json `articles`, `jobs.kindRuns.articles`).
The runner's `orbit wiki articles` (src/runner-go/wiki_articles_test.go, TestWikiArticleAsksWhatTheServerAsks) and the
server's `articles` job (src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-articles-job.spec.ts, wiki-articles-writer.spec.ts) are each run
on `topics` with the model answering as `model` says, and each must ask exactly `calls` — every prompt, word for word,
by the unit the server files it under — and group the big topic exactly as `groups` says, entry for entry.
`model`: the nth prompt that asks for a group's name is answered `names[n]` wrapped as a model wraps a short answer
(`OK, the subheading for this group is:\n"…"`); a prompt that asks for an article again (`A previous draft kept only`) is answered
`article`; any other prompt for an article titled `shortFor` is answered `short` (so that topic is asked twice), and every
other article `article`, which keeps more than rules.minChars.
`calls` and `groups` are written by the runner: `go test -run TestWikiArticleAsksWhatTheServerAsks
-update-wiki-article-writer-fixture` from src/runner-go. Change a prompt on one side and the other side's test says so.

model.article:
# How articles are written

An article is made only of sentences the server has checked, and every sentence carries a footnote[1]. A topic whose fingerprint has not changed is not written again[2].

## Conventions

Before a write, the fingerprint of the entry set is checked, and if it differs nothing is written at all[1][3]. Grouping looks at the anchor paths first, then at the words of the titles and summaries[2].
Each group is written from at most thirty entries, those with the most sources, and the rest stay out of the prompt[3]. What runs past nine hundred characters is cut by the server from the end of the longest section[1].

## Common pitfalls

If the entries change while the model is writing, the write is refused, and the next run writes again from the new entries[2]. A sentence without a footnote is deleted, so every sentence carries its number[3].
The names of one topic's groups must differ, or a reader cannot tell what each article is about[1]. Code goes in backticks, such as `arr[0]`, and the brackets inside it are no footnote[2].

## Practice

First read the topic's plan, and write only the topics whose entry set changed, leaving the unchanged ones as they are[1]. A big topic is grouped by its anchor paths first, and each group is given a name different from every other group's[2].
Each group gets a subtopic article and the overview comes last, written only from the two entries with the most sources in each group[3]. What is written goes to the server to be checked, and the server keeps only the sentences whose footnotes point at the topic's entries[1][2].

## Decisions

Every model call goes through a persisted request queue, so a call already answered is not asked again after a restart[3]. An article records the commit of the repository snapshot it was written at, so a reader can tell which version of the code it describes[1].
